ambiguities.description: Tax ID is mentioned as an attribute of Vendor but is explicitly NOT unique (duplicate vendors can share a tax ID). Should Tax ID be modeled as a plain value type attribute with no uniqueness, and should the duplicate-vendor cleanup issue be tracked separately? Confirm Tax ID has no uniqueness constraint at all.

source_references.excerpt:
Facilitator: And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?
Dana: You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

ambiguities.description: Vendor has three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) which are 'frequently different'. It's unclear whether these should be modeled as three separate value types/roles on Vendor, or as a single Address entity type with an AddressType classification. Granularity of address structure (street/city/etc.) is also unaddressed.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: 'Tier' is an overloaded term -- Procurement uses it for spend tier (bronze/silver/gold) and Compliance uses it for risk tier (low/medium/high). Confirmed as two separate fields per the transcript, but the naming collision itself is flagged as an ongoing organizational ambiguity/risk that should be surfaced in documentation.

source_references.excerpt: Raj: We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos. Someone says "that's a high tier vendor" in a meeting and half the room hears "big spender" and the other half hears "dangerous," and those are very different conversations.

ambiguities.description: Post-suspension handling of in-flight Purchase Orders (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly parked/undecided pending a steering group and Legal review. No constraint should be modeled for this until resolved.

source_references.excerpt: Facilitator: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided. Today's model captures three statuses and the creation-time control, and nothing about post-suspension fulfilment, because there is nothing agreed to capture.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag exists informally in Mei's personal spreadsheet with no defined selection rule or process; explicitly declared out of scope and not to be modeled ('ad hoc, don't model it'). Flagging to confirm it remains excluded from the formal model.

source_references.excerpt: Mei: It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Region set (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM) is described as fixed today but with an open possibility of splitting EMEA in the future. Should the value_constraint on RegionCode be treated as closed/stable or should Region be modeled as an open entity type to accommodate future splits?

source_references.excerpt:
Mei: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.
Facilitator: Four regions, fixed?
Mei: Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Temporal/historical tracking: risk reviews accumulate over time ('a vendor accumulates review records over time... at most one is the current one') but the transcript doesn't specify how 'current' is determined (e.g., a status flag, date range) versus historical reviews. The model needs an explicit attribute (e.g., IsCurrent or ReviewStatus) to distinguish current vs past reviews, which is only implied.

source_references.excerpt: Raj: A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Contact is described only via Name, Email, Phone Number with no reference_mode/identifier discussed. It's unclear how a Contact would be uniquely identified independent of the Vendor+Region pairing (e.g., is Contact its own entity with an ID, or purely a value cluster attached to the Vendor-Region fact)? Currently modeled as an attribute-holding entity identified indirectly by the Vendor+Region uniqueness, which may need clarification.

source_references.excerpt:

...A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.
